utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Since the court deputy is not with us, I will read out the case number. It is case number IT-95-16-T, The Prosecutor against Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic. We will now continue, and I hope you don't have any exhibits to tender into evidence because, for the time being, we are without the court deputy. Oh, all right. He is here. Everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cilic. If you agree, we will resume where we left off at the end of the last sitting. You remember that we began to talk about the 15th of April, 1993. In the course of your testimony, a video film was shown at the time that Commander Totic was kidnapped and his escort assassinated. Of course, you don't have that video before you now and you didn't participate in the investigation, if there was one, but in view of your position, did you learn anything about the circumstances of that operation?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, I did not participate in the investigation nor was I on the spot nor did I learn any particular details regarding the investigation except for the fact that the commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade from Zenica was alive. We learnt that as early as the 16th in the afternoon. At the time, I didn't have any additional information about that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Commander Totic, did he reappear a couple of days later?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I think he appeared after more than a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And when he did reappear, did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I met him in Vitez several days later because after his release, he came to Vitez, because a number of the members of the brigade of which he was in command had, under threat of force by the BH army, fled from Zenica to the Lasva Valley, and this meant also to the territory of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you met Commander Totic, did he explain to you what had happened?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not to me personally, because we knew each other very superficially, but he tried to explain it in a short statement for the viewers of the local TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What do you remember of those explanations that he gave?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember much, but I will tell you what I do remember in brief. Totic said that together with his escort, he had started out from Zenica, as he did every day, to the command of his brigade which was situated in a suburb called Podbrezje. On the road close to his command, a group of armed and masked soldiers intercepted them, stopped their car, dragged him out of the car, and then, with a burst of fire, killed his escort. At the time, he wasn't able to say that a chance passerby was also killed on that occasion. That is as much as I can tell you about that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Commander Totic did not give you any explanation why this operation was conducted in particular against him and his escort?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He didn't tell me nor the local TV programme, but I assume he did give such explanations in the appropriate place. A local media is not such an appropriate place, at least that is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I understand. The names of the members of the escort of Commander Totic, were they conveyed on television, according to the transcript before yesterday, Ivica Vidovic, Anto Zrnic, Marko and Tihomir Ljubic. Those were the names we received. Do you know them?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were they local people, as far as you know, people from the area of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not one of them was from the area of Vitez, as far as I know. All four came from the territory of Zenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let us now go on to the press conference, if you don't mind, an abstract of which we saw the day before yesterday during your testimony. In the course of that press conference, we saw a young woman reading a list of operations attributed to the Bosnian army, a list clearly carefully prepared, and the film stopped there. Could you specify the time of that press conference?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not with precision, I'm not sure whether it was at 11.00 or at 12.00, but either one of those times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, after this list was read, as we saw on the videotape, who took the floor after that and to say what?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether the first speaker after that was Colonel Tihomir Blaskic or Mr. Dario Kordic, but I don't think that is so important, which one spoke first, but I do know that both of them spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What is important, perhaps, is to know what they said. You were present during that press conference?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and, of course, after so much time has gone by, I cannot recall in detail exactly what they said, but I certainly can give you the main points.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, please, do that.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I shall try to give you a summary which can be said to cover the points made by both. They elaborated on all those events covering the period roughly from the New Year until the 15th of April, 1993, indicating the constant and repeated incidents being provoked by members of the BH army, the victims being mostly members of the Croatian Defence Council. They also, and Mr. Dario Kordic in particular, indicated that they had reported to all the competent and relevant institutions about those events, representatives of the political and military field as well as members of the International Community. Mr. Blaskic said, roughly, that the HVO forces were against any kind of conflict but that they would have to defend themselves if necessary. They roughly said, We will certainly not bend down but we will defend ourselves if our integrity in this area is jeopardised. That would roughly be the summary, but, Mr. Prosecutor, please take this with a little reservation because this was too long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could it be said that the general meaning of that press conference, its justification, was to prepare the Croatian community for war?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not how I experienced it, and at the time, I never even dreamt that we were only a couple of hours away from war. There were warnings that there should be a maximum degree of caution and responsibility of each and every individual everywhere, but I did not see it as being the last prior to a bloody war. Allow me to add that the atmosphere was very tolerant, and in some senses, its aim was to calm people down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you think that the reading that we heard of the list of aggressive acts allegedly committed by the BH army from the beginning of the year until the 15th of April had an appeasing effect on the Croatian community?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't mean that. What I meant was that the statements made by our most prominent figures in military and civilian life, in my judgment, were not inflammatory, there were no threats, and, of course, those events could not have an appeasing effect, but I must also say that similar enumerations of incidents and crimes committed had been made earlier on, not to such an extent, because these press conferences and these data covered a relatively long period of time, so that necessarily the list of incidents and crimes was far longer than at earlier press conferences.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: This press conference, was it broadcast live on television?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we didn't have the necessary resources for live transmissions. We were under total information blockade, and our local television was an improvised station as compared to the large information machinery at the disposal of the Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Under those conditions, could you tell us when this press conference was broadcast on television for the Croatian community?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 7.00 p.m. This was the customary and only time that we had on local television for our news programs. On the Vitez radio, at 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us, in the course of your testimony, that towards the end of the afternoon of the 15th of April, you went to Zenica by car to find your daughter there who was studying in that town. If I understood well your statement, but please correct me if I'm wrong, on the road you encountered a certain number of roadblocks. All those roadblocks were either held by the HVO or by the civilian police. You did not encounter, on the road going from Vitez to Zenica, the Bosnian army. Is that correct? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not quite. On the road from Vitez to Zenica, there wasn't a single roadblock put up and held by HVO members.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, these roadblocks were held by the civilian police. I think you also spoke of the HOS having barricades. But the gist of my question is that the Bosnian army was not present on the road until the very entrance into Zenica. You also told us, and again correct me if I'm wrong, that in the town of Zenica itself, you did not witness any major presence of the Bosnian army with the exception of a few trucks passing by.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the road, I didn't see anywhere members of the BH army, on the road from Vitez to Zenica. I am referring to the roadblocks. Nor did I see any members of the HVO. At the first roadblock, I saw a civilian policeman belonging to the Vitez police station, the Croatian part of the station; then the second barricade was held by civilian policemen also belonging to the Vitez station, but this time to the Muslim part; and a third roadblock was held only by HOS members; and then came roadblocks manned by policemen with helmets and armed to the teeth. At the time, these were members of the Muslim police in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you returned to Vitez, that was the same evening?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, about 1900 hours, I think I was already back in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You came back accompanied by your daughter, together with your daughter?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was lucky enough to bring my daughter home. I took her to our apartment, and then I returned to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were you going to report to the commander of what you saw on the road going to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I reported orally in detail to the commander, Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What was the gist of that report? Was it, as one might think, bearing in mind what you said that you saw, that, in fact, there was very little activity by the Bosnian army in that region?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In addition to my impressions as a parent and my happiness at having brought back my daughter, I reported everything I said here two days ago, maybe in somewhat greater detail, and what I tried to repeat this morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, my question was as follows: What was the meaning of your report? Was it reassuring in the sense that there was a little activity of the Bosnian army in that area from Vitez to Zenica, or, on the contrary, was your report disturbing, alarming?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that after everything I saw and experienced, of course, it couldn't be reassuring. I was particularly surprised by the situation in Zenica. The impression was as if it was 2.00 a.m. rather than 4.00 or 5.00 in the afternoon. Zenica is a workers' city and a centre, a large city, relatively speaking, with many students and school children, and it is a city always alive, buzzing, as if in a beehive, and though it was a nice day, the town was literally deserted, even though it was the early afternoon, and that is why I noticed several vehicles of the BH army and far more policemen than is customary, and this time, armed to the teeth with automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 334, Exhibit 334.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, this document appears to be a military report characterised as strictly confidential, drafted by the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica, 16th of April. No time is indicated. Anyway, no hour can be read on this document. Nevertheless, it appears that this document relates to the situation such as it was at 6.00 a.m. on the 16th of April. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The situation described on the 16th of April at 6.00, is it a situation that can be considered normal under the circumstances in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time? The situation was calm, there were no combat operations, the night was quiet and civilians could go to work.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That would be the conclusion one could draw from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, I want to show you another document, and we will pass on to another area of your testimony now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 335.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, can you identify the heading of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which was the authority that drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was drafted by the Defence Department of Vitez municipality, and as far as I can see it was signed by the leader of that department, that is Marijan Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: It appears to be dated the end of April, April 1993 if we read the date on the left, and it was registered in Travnik, in any event, on the 30th of April, 1993. That can be seen on the first page, the date when it was registered in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, though the number is not quite legible. I think it is the 29th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I should like to draw your attention to page 1 and point 3, but I must note that there are two paragraphs 3. This must be an error in the numbering, but I'm interested in the second paragraph number 3. It says in this paragraph that from the 16th of April until the 28th of April, 1993, a total of 498 conscripts were mobilised and actively included in the HVO forces, in addition to the regular personnel of the Vitez Brigade. It also says that the majority of conscripts mobilised since the outbreak of hostilities were directly sent to the defence lines. Could you please look through the rest of this document quickly, the following pages of this document, and I draw your attention to numbers 106, 107 and 109. What names do you find there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Under number 106 is Zoran Kupreskic, 107 is Vlatko Kupreskic, and 109 Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I now draw your attention to numbers 343 and 349. What names do you see there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: 343 is Drago Josipovic, and 349 Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I ask you now to go back to numbers 96, 97, 98. On the right-hand side there is a date indicated, a number. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Are you speaking about number 81?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Facing the names, opposite 84 and 88 there is a note. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm not able to decipher this. For me this is something new, I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: This means that there was the co-operation of these persons who are mentioned, that were reported on the 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, one could conclude so because it says "from" before the date, so that is the conclusion that one could draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On that same page, the last name, the name 149, there is a mention there in the area. On the same page, Mr. Usher. 149, there is another name listed there. What name is that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is probably a person who was old enough when he could not be mobilised any more according to the existing laws, and I believe that that's probably what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A little further down, unfortunately I cannot tell you what page number it is because it's a document which bears a number 67, but later on -- below that, actually, it is mentioned -- or two names are mentioned as having a particular assignment. This is on page 29.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sir, I don't have page numbers, so could you help me in another way to locate this place?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. In the upper right-hand side of each page there is a number.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There aren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I'm sorry. Excuse me. Now, on this page, which is the English version with the number 29 marked, are there not names mentioned, names of persons who were made active -- put into active service in the HVO to do a particular type of assignment, and who were deployed through other means than the normal armed forces? In this case, involving the logistics.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There are three such remarks. One is under 10. This would be "Work duty," "Special purposes." Also, there is "Work unit" and "Logistics." I assume that these are the duties that you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, can it be said that the names are --

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you will just give me enough time to go over the entire list, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, I've noted that not all of your question was put into English in the transcript. Perhaps if you could repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I will repeat it. I asked the witness whether or not he was in agreement with me to note that the names of the accused do not appear under this particular title "Special purposes."

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can answer that question, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No name was mentioned of the persons who are sitting here and who stand accused. However, on the basis of this list, I can conclude that these are mostly elderly people or people with certain health conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: With your permission, Mr. Cilic, since the date of birth located across from each name, all of them are of an elderly age, since some of them were born in 1950, '56. So these are persons are not necessarily of an elderly age, perhaps given their state of health, but consequently, Mr. Cilic, I would have to conclude, from this document that the accused who we have listed earlier were all located on the date of April 1993 in a mobilised state and on active members of the HVO on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Ms. Glumac, do you have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just like to point out that the Prosecutor is showing the witness this list. However, the fact is that in the first part it states that this is a period of between 16 and 28th of April when 498 persons were mobilised, so this in itself prevents this witness to conclude that all these persons were mobilised on the 16th of April, because that is something that is mentioned in the preamble of this document, and I think that this is an improper way of asking this question, because it is contrary to what is stated in the text of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, Madam, I'm not in agreement with you at all, because the Prosecutor, Mr. Terrier, has indeed asked questions with regard to the names on the list in relation to which the list specifies that they were mobilised from the 16th of April. So he's asking a question based on a logical deduction from this. I believe the question is admissible and Mr. Terrier is right to ask it. I would now request that the witness answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Clearly, Mr. President, it's the Tribunal that will have to ascertain the weight of this document, but I will ask for the witness to give his point of view on this document, the document he has before him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can you not tell us whether or not the accused, whose names were already given, are all listed under the date of the 16th of April, 1993 shown as having been mobilised in active service of the HVO army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, I believe there is an objection from Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that the question asked by the Prosecution is a leading question. It suggests the 16th of April. I think that we need to determine on which dates these persons who are on the list were mobilised. So I second the objection by Madam Slokovic-Glumac, because the mobilisation covers the period between 16th and 28th of April. So my objection is that the question should not be whether they were also mobilised on the 16th but when these persons were mobilised, on what date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The question that the Prosecutor has asked is not whether the accused were mobilised on the 16th, because obviously the witness cannot know this, but it's based on this document. In any case the objection cannot be sustained, although I do not lend too much weight to this, because as the Prosecutor says, it is up to the Court to read the document and to give the proper deductions that it may give and the weight that is necessary. Mr. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witnesses should testify to what they know, not what their opinions of certain documents may be, so that would be the proper way of examining them. So if we asked them such questions it would be -- it is not what is pertinent to their testimony. However, let me draw your attention to a fact which is especially significant in this document, and which is disregarded by the Prosecutor when examining the witness and has not asked this witness any questions of. In this document, it is stated explicitly that the military personnel mobilised was -- were used as replacement after the first attack. In other words, that they were gradually brought in as replacement -- as a reserve. And if we interpret this correctly, that means that these persons were introduced in the frontlines only after the first attack and when the first professional HVO soldiers were replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Radovic just dictated his statement to the witness. I would like, nonetheless, with your permission, to ask a question to this witness in regards to this document, which I believe has a certain amount of importance with regards to this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, you are a very informed person about the military situation. Does this document not signify that on the 16th of April, in any case, until the 20th of April, that the persons who we have named and the persons accused in the context of this trial were indeed mobilised in active service of the HVO army?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can confirm only, in other words, affirmatively only to part of your question. I cannot tell you that they were all mobilised on the 16th but that they were all active until the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Not indicated in the later part of this document that most of these persons mobilised since the start of the hostilities were sent to the first line of defence. It's on the same page, Mr. Cilic, just later on on that same page of the text.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, up until that date, and one could conclude that they were a replacement of the HVO soldiers who had been on the frontlines up until that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have finished with this document. I would like now to address another issue of your testimony. You stated to us on Wednesday that you learned what occurred in Ahmici three days later and that what you had learned shocked you a great deal and that you spoke about what happened in Ahmici as being a crime. This is the word you used, and this is found in the transcript. I would like for you to tell us what type of information you received which led you to think that a crime had been committed in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that on the third or fourth day, a number of the Muslims who were killed from Ahmici were exchanged, which was covered by our local television. I also believe that on one of these days, I saw a brief report -- and I'm not sure whether this was on CNN or BBC, but it was an international television outlet -- and it dispelled any doubts that there had been a crime committed in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were you in possession of other information apart from those which were given by television or radio? Would you yourself be in possession of information? Did this information contain other facts than those?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean specifically Ahmici or the entire Vitez municipality area, because crimes were committed ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Right now, I'm referring to the crimes which you refer to as having been committed in Ahmici in particular.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really did not have more details. I could not have had more details because immediately after that horrible event, this area was completely blocked by the UNPROFOR units of the British battalion, so it was impossible to go there and record any videotape or gather any additional information. Only some international television outlets were allowed to do so, and even they selectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you stated that the British battalion, located in Vitez, blocked the road leading to Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. My information was that as a member of the Croatian Defence Council, and this also included staff of the local radio and television stations, were not allowed into Ahmici; in other words, we had no access there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You were very well-informed, were you not, of the military operations on the 16th of April and the days that followed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how much information I did have at that time, but obviously I did know certain things. Of course. I had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can it be said that you were directly involved in this military operation?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Fortunately, no, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, I would like to submit to you another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 336.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, are you indeed the person who signed this report?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You mention, as a duty officer, you signed this document --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, my apologies. One moment, please. We have great difficulty reading the Croatian version. Could the witness please be given more time, because it is hardly legible at all? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you indeed sign this document as the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: This document is dated the 17th of April at 6.00 a.m. Were you indeed the duty officer at that time, and if so, at what time and when did you begin this service?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think that I would have recalled it had you not given me this document, but you can conclude from this that I was the duty officer during the 17th; in other words, on the night between the 16th and the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it not the duty of a duty officer, when he takes his office, to be informed of the situation on the ground and to gather all available information?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On this particular night, the entire command staff of the Viteska Brigade was in the headquarters, and I only drafted this report but, of course, I do not deny it because I signed it. However, it is easy to conclude from this report that it was drafted based on the information and data received during the night at the headquarters, and this report is a sum of all the pieces of information which myself and the other staff, command staff, received in the course of that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, since it appears from this document that you were very directly implicated in this military operation, I am going to ask you if you did not receive some intelligence about what had happened in Ahmici through those means.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not receive any information because I was a member of the Viteska Brigade command which had no activities, ongoing activities, in Ahmici on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What about other Croatian officials apart from you that said that a crime had been committed in Ahmici? Do you recall that, that anyone else said that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would not like to speak on behalf of others, but I can tell you that no man of reason could have described that in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you recall a Croatian official from the region publicly identifying the perpetrators of those crimes?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not recall anyone doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about names of individuals but military units.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Regarding this event, this crime in Ahmici, for a long time and to this day, there has been a great deal of speculation and various rumours have been circulating about this crime, so that to tell you quite frankly, I wouldn't like to get involved in those speculations. I simply had no information that I could claim was correct as to who had committed the crime in Ahmici. All that I can explicitly say is that it was not committed by members of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Going back to this document that you signed as duty officer on the 17th of April at 6.00 a.m., and I draw your attention to the third paragraph. Have you had time to read it in the original version?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Are you referring to this paragraph referring to Grbavica and the Mujahedins?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No, where reference is made to Rovna, Santici, and Ahmici, that paragraph. Santici and Ahmici are, in fact, underlined. It is the third paragraph. Yes? Have you had time to read it? Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have now, though it is very difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Nonetheless, could we not conclude from this paragraph, of which you are the author, that, in the course of the night, that is the night that preceded the writing of this report, this means the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, information about the regrouping of Muslim forces from which you conclude that those forces are going to make an attempt to break through from Vrhovine in the direction of Santici and Ahmici? Should we not conclude from that, and I'm asking your opinion as the author of this document, that at the time it was written, the 17th of April at 6.00 in the morning, there was no conflict yet in the region of Ahmici and Santici for control of the Vitez-Busovaca road?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The crime committed in Ahmici was committed on the 16th, so that we cannot say that there was no fighting in Ahmici until then. And the terminology used here is quite alien to me. But I told you that all of us members of the command were in the headquarters that night, and it was not a question of a single officer on duty, regardless of the fact that I signed this document, but I am not trying to avoid responsibility for this report. But the professional and competent people, far more competent people for military affairs, participated in its drafting, more competent than I was then and than I am now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, allow me to note nevertheless that there is a difference between combat and a crime, on the one hand; and that, on the other, you are a journalist by profession, a specialist in information and you are familiar with language, and you are also perfectly informed of the military situation as you were an officer on duty. Therefore, it seems to me that what you wrote has a meaning, that what you wrote was based on information that you had collected and certainly verified, and the date and hour when you wrote this report, judging from this report, it would appear that no military conflict had occurred in the region of Santici or Ahmici for the control of the Vitez-Busovaca road.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were battles ongoing all the time of greater or lesser intensity, and one couldn't say that there were any number of hours when there was no fighting in this area. Here reference is made to regrouping of larger forces, which was a threat to the HVO, and the threat existed of intercepting communications which were of vital importance for the population of the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, since you were the author of this report, and perhaps other reports of a similar kind, and this report has a reference which is similar to the reference found on documents already admitted into evidence and conveyed during your testimony, you are probably familiar with these administrative matters, so could you explain to us, what is the significance of this reference number, referring to this document again, the number that can be found at the top of the page on your document? In this case, the number is 02-125-16/93.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my statement -- or, actually, during the examination-in-chief, I said that I am not familiar with the methodology of registering documents, but the date here is quite clear and the hour is quite clear, so I think there can be no dilemmas in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I am not doubting the authenticity of this document, I was just asking whether you could explain how these numbers were made and what significance they have. Is there a reference to the department? Is there a reference to chronology? Was there a sequence, an order, in which various documents were drafted and how these numbers were attached, affixed? If you don't know, you don't know, Mr. Cilic.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really do not know the answer to that question. There is no reason why I wouldn't tell you, but I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Fine. I should now like to show the witness document D39/2. Mr. Cilic, this is a document that you have seen because it was admitted into evidence during your examination-in-chief. I should like to draw your attention to the name Livancic, Zeljo. The person has died. He was a member of the Vitez Brigade. Did you know when this person was killed and under what circumstances, or how the person died?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know when the person died. I think even that I put a question mark as to whether he, in fact, was a member of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I am going to show you another document referring to the same issue, that is, the victims of the conflict that were engaged as members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 337.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, referring to the Croatian version, can you tell us whether you knew which authority drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is not difficult to gather from the heading. It is clear that the document was issued by the Defence office or department of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that this document contains a list of members of the HVO who were killed in the course of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I must make a reservation here because I think you're overestimating my ability to confirm all these names and dates because -- out of respect for you and their Honours, I do not wish to claim "Yes" or "No." I really do not have a computer in my brain, so I can't give you a very specific answer. But, at the same time, I wouldn't call in doubt this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, it goes without saying that I'm not asking you to confirm whether all the information contained in this report is authentic or not. That would not be serious on my part. So please feel at ease. I am just referring to your experience, your professional experience from the period. You identified the body or the authority issuing this document. I would just like us to look at it together and review some aspects of it, and I would like you to tell me, because I am looking at the English version, whether you agree that on the left-hand side there is a number, then there's a name, then the year of birth of that person, then the date of that person's death, then the place of death, then the address, his residence before death, then the place, sometimes the date of burial, and in some cases a comment regarding the person or the circumstances under which he was killed. I draw your attention, and it may be rather sensitive to refer to numbers, but on page 3 there's a name figuring opposite the number 160. Would you agree with me in saying that this name is the name of Livancic, father's name Jozo, first name Zeljo?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that according to this document, that person died on the 18th of April, 1993 at Kuber and came originally from Santici?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Though the date appears to have been corrected, but I think it is legible as 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I don't see that it has been corrected. It was underlined in the original, and we can still see traces of the underlining on the copy. This document was submitted by the Defence of Colonel Blaskic in the Blaskic case. I now wish to draw your attention to page 8 of this same document. Look at number 413 and 414, and we'll see two names there. According to this document, both of these persons died on the 18th of April, 1993 in Kuber, both of them came from Santici. Are we in agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A minor correction. They didn't die, these persons are missing and they have never been traced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Can one conclude, Mr. Cilic, from this document that a conflict did indeed occur in Kuber but on the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At Kuber, and this is something I referred to in my testimony, Kuber was one of the most important and dominant features in the area, and it dominates over Zenica, Busovaca and Vitez. And the first conflict and the first wounding of Croatian soldiers at Kuber were recorded on the 15th of April, 1993 in the afternoon hours, in the early afternoon. At the time already, the BH army, in an armed attack, provoked a serious incident and wounded two soldiers. I'm not sure, but I think one of them died later, but this is not something I can claim with certainty. I must also say that already on the first day of the conflict, when the conflict escalated on the 16th, the Muslim forces captured the peak of Kuber, which had been held until then mostly by units from Busovaca and also by some smaller units from Vitez. They also captured another important feature, Brdo, in the north the municipality, and chased away from there the Croatian inhabitants and set light to Croatian homes. If we add to this that on the same day, a very important -- a strategically important village, the village of Poculica, was captured by Muslim forces where several civilians were killed and dozens of Croatian houses burnt. By the 16th they had gained control of the most dominant features in the north of Vitez municipality. So it can be said that already on that day the Lasva River Valley, or, rather, the territory of Vitez municipality was at close reach.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, under those conditions would you say -- you may believe me or not, but the document is at the disposal of the Judges and each one of the attorneys. In this document we cannot find a single victim killed on the 15th or the 16th of April at Kuber. On the other hand, there is mention of three persons who fell as victims of a conflict on the 18th at Kuber. How is it possible that if we look at all the victims of the 16th of April we find three names? No one, no member of the HVO, was killed during conflicts, if there were conflicts, in Ahmici or at Kuber. Could we not think, in view of the information appearing in this document and you identified the origins of, that what happened on the 15th or the 16th of April, that is the Thursday or Friday, in fact happened on Sunday or Monday, the 18th or 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to information that I have, the two persons that you have referred to, I think it was Grgic and Livancic, these two disappeared on the 16th. However, their disappearance was reported on the 18th, and then that day was registered as the day when they were registered as missing. You must understand that in those circumstances of the escalation of the war, the information reaching these institutions and other organisations were not always correct nor timely, and there are certainly a number of errors here which it will take time to correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I have almost finished. I should like to touch upon another area of your testimony. You spoke of your meeting with Dr. Mujezinovic. Dr. Mujezinovic was a witness at The Hague Tribunal within two proceedings, the case against Tihomir Blaskic and the case against Anto Furundzija. In both cases, he described this meeting with Mario Cerkez, of which you were an eyewitness, and it is in this connection that I should like to hear your opinion and ask you to refer to your memories. In both cases Dr. Mujezinovic did not describe the same facts as you did. With your permission, allow me to summarise his testimony and to underline the main points of his statement. According to Dr. Mujezinovic, the following happened: On Monday, the 19th of April, 1993, very early in the morning he was in the hospital healing the wounded and the sick that he was responsible for, and he was taken into custody by HVO soldiers. He was taken to the cinema hall that you mentioned, and taken before Mario Cerkez. You were present when he appeared, if I may call it that, this appearance of Dr. Mujezinovic. He was present, you were present, together with other people belonging to the HVO. You were in uniform. You were carrying the HVO insignia. Is that correct up to correct up to this point? What was the meaning of this interview between Dr. Mujezinovic with Mario Cerkez? According to Dr. Mujezinovic, Mario Cerkez said the following: He asked Dr. Mujezinovic, "Have you heard talk about Ahmici?" on the 19th, Monday the 19th. The crime in Ahmici had occurred the previous Friday. "Have you heard talk about Ahmici?" Dr. Mujezinovic answered yes, that he actually knew what had happened. At least that he had some information as to what had happened. At that point Mario Cerkez said, "You must do what we are telling you to do." Then Mario Cerkez asked Dr. Mujezinovic to call a certain number of his acquaintances, especially Muslim officials, to tell them that if the Bosnian army advanced in the direction of Vitez, they must know that he, Mario Cerkez, and the HVO has 2.223 captured Muslims, mostly women and children, and that he would kill them all. Is this correct? Did Mario Cerkez say this to Dr. Mujezinovic in your presence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't -- I was not present when such a conversation took place. Mario did not say that to Dr. Mujezinovic. And at the beginning of your summary regarding the arrival of Dr. Muhamed to the command was, in fact, different, because I participated. He was not brought in from the health centre --

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Cilic. You can't say at the same time that you were not present during this conversation and say at the same time that Mario Cerkez did not say that. Either you were present and you know what was said, or you were not present and you don't know what was said.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that I was not present at a meeting where such words were uttered. Maybe there was another meeting, another encounter, but I know very well and in detail what happened, because I stated clearly that Muhamed is a friend of mine, and that I undertook this gesture towards Muhamed and that's why I remember very well each and every detail. Therefore, I appeal to you to hear me out when I say that Dr. Muhamed was not brought to Mario Cerkez from the health centre. This may have been another occasion when he was taken into custody. He was, in fact, brought from the cinema hall where he had already been all day in detention. And upon my insistence twice with Mario, Mario agreed that I bring Dr. Mujezinovic from that detention area to see him, and then to take him home, and then the next day Muhamed went to work in the health centre. So that I appeal to you, Mr. Prosecutor, not to get the impression that I'm trying to avoid an answer to your question, but I'm just saying that there may have been another interview between Mario and Dr. Mujezinovic which I did not attend, because such threats and such wording was not used by Mario when I was present and when he was talking to Dr. Mujezinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I was just referring to the statements made twice in this Tribunal by Dr. Mujezinovic, according to which these meetings were held in your presence and the presence of other persons whom he mentions, whose names he mentions, and that you were wearing a uniform with HVO insignia. Dr. Mujezinovic continues his testimony as follows: Mario Cerkez asked Dr. Mujezinovic to make contact with various Muslim officials, to inform them of this threat to kill all the hostages, if we can call them that, and asks you, Mr. Cilic, to actually conduct these negotiations, which you did. Dr. Mujezinovic contacted various Muslim officials, conveying to them the threat made by Mario Cerkez to kill the hostages, and Mr. Mujezinovic, accompanied by you yourself, had to return to the detention centre, we're still talking about Monday, the 19th of April, to form a group of Muslims who would be asked to negotiate, if we can call these negotiations, with the HVO authorities. At the time there were about 300 detainees in the cinema hall; is that correct? If anything I'm saying is incorrect, please say so.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I was just going to ask you, if I may, to convey my impressions of what happened. In my presence, and I brought Dr. Mujezinovic from the cinema hall to the command of the Vitez Brigade, that means only a floor above. Dr. Muhamed shook hands very cordially with the commander of the Vitez Brigade, Mario Cerkez. He had a strong drink with Mario. I did not have a drink because I do -- I abstain from taking alcohol. He also had a cup of coffee. They discussed a report broadcast by television Sarajevo on that day, that is that a prominent physician, a specialist, a prominent citizen and a senior official of the SDA, Dr. Muhamed Mujezinovic, had been killed in Vitez that day. He was not aware of this report. There was no reference in my presence to Ahmici, and I was there all the time throughout that interview, from the time Dr. Muhamed Mujezinovic came to the command until he left to go home, and not to go back into detention. The officials of the political authorities in Vitez and Mario Cerkez asked Dr. Muhamed, bearing in mind his prestige in political circles, as well as in military circles and especially among the ordinary citizens, that he use his influence to affect a cessation of shelling of inhabited areas and especially the city centre. It was said that there was a threat, a danger, that some of the people who had fled from Zenica and whose houses had been burned, who had lost their closest relatives, could provoke a very serious incident, because in two or three locations large groups of Muslims were being held in detention, but under no circumstances was it said that anybody would intentionally kill people if they didn't see the shelling. This is something I claim explicitly under full moral and material responsibility in this honourable Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, do you have many more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: No, not many. Another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So you said that you were present, but Mario Cerkez did not make the threats that Dr. Mujezinovic reports. Dr. Mujezinovic also said, and I should like to hear your opinion, this is perhaps a little far removed from our subject, that there were 300 Muslims detained in the cinema under conditions which he found to be extremely difficult. That is, it was cold there and many of the people were sick. He said that he made a list of 20 persons that needed to be released immediately in view of their state of health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Objection on the part of Ms. Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are having a bit of -- some difficulty following the Prosecutor. He's using a testimony from another case, and he's quoting parts and reading, so it is very difficult to follow because we are not familiar with the totality of that statement. So we're finding it difficult to follow. In fact, we were not told that the testimony of another witness would be used from another case in such detail. So I think it is difficult for us to follow and for the witness in particular. So I object to this method of cross-examination. I apologise. The witness has already -- the witness has already recounted in detail his encounter with Dr. Mujezinovic, so this is actually repetition and reference to a testimony that we -- that is not at our disposal. Thank you. That is not available to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It is our judgment that Ms. Slokovic-Glumac is right. The Defence was not able to have the text of this testimony of Dr. Mujezinovic in another case. But if you intend to continue along this line of questioning, then the Defence should have the relevant testimony. Are you insisting on this point or could you perhaps conclude with your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The Prosecution finds itself in the following situation: In the course of his testimony, Mr. Cilic recounted an encounter with Dr. Mujezinovic, a meeting which the Prosecution considers to be very important for the situation at the time. Dr. Mujezinovic, on the other hand, twice in two different trials, recounted the same event but in a different way, and I'm referring to one of the statements he made, the one he made in the trial of Dr. Blaskic. Perhaps we can suspend for a few minutes and I will communicate to the Defence this statement so that the rights of the Defence are fully observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We're going to suspend now for 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 338.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are now looking at a transcript of testimony given by Dr. Mujezinovic on the 20th of August --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we only have just received the transcript this very moment, that is, the statement of Dr. Mujezinovic. In order to be able to follow the questions, we at least need to be able to read through this document; otherwise, it's as if we had never received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, I hope to be able to go over it very quickly. Mr. President, I indicated to Defence counsel that the passages of interest to us here are the following: From line 22 on page of 164 in which Dr. Mujezinovic relates what happened on Monday, the 19th of April; and from page 1.706, line 8, here he relates what Mr. Mario Cerkez told him in the presence of Mr. Cilic. The effective presence of Mr. Cilic is mentioned by Dr. Mujezinovic on 1.705, on line 17. Therefore, this will enable Defence counsel to be able to quickly take knowledge of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now give Defence counsel some time, and in the meantime, has the witness received the text and is it in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it is in English. As you know, we do not have it in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Therefore, I believe you should read the relevant passage so that it can be translated into Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, unless, of course, you do so, I have no intention of coming back to what we have already discussed, that is to say, what Mr. Mario Cerkez stated in the presence or outside of the presence of the witness, according to his own memory. The witness does not confirm the statements made by Dr. Mujezinovic. I do not intend on insisting, unless, of course, you insist that I come back to this issue, but I simply wish to go further on in the testimony about this meeting with Mr. Cilic and Dr. Mujezinovic and raise the question of the Muslim prisoners who were located in the movie hall. This question was raised from page 1.709 of the transcript. For the attention of Mr. Cilic and with your permission, Mr. President, while the Defence counsel are taking cognisance of this transcript, I would perhaps like to summarise what Dr. Mujezinovic stated under your own supervision, under the supervision of Your Honours, and also the Defence counsel here present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Dr. Mujezinovic, Mr. Cilic, states that they went into the basement of this movie hall, and there discovered that at a location which was used to store coal, there was a large number of persons detained. He lists a number of 300 persons on page 1.710, on line 14. He states that among these 300 persons who were located there on the 19th of April and detained in that location, there were a number of sick persons, and these persons were chronically ill. Dr. Mujezinovic states that he made a list of these ill persons, and he states in the transcript on page 1.710, on line 20, that when he knew that you were going to work together -- since he knew you were working as a social worker, he gave you a list of the 20 chronic patients for them to be freed. He states he does not know whether that was done. And the question is the following: Do you recall Dr. Mujezinovic drafted a list of 20 persons who were ill and in detention for whom he recommended their release, and do you recall this list?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that Dr. Mujezinovic gave a list. In fact, he asked of Mr. Mario Cerkez to allow him to compile this list. Then he compiled it and handed it to Mr. Cerkez. I was present when he compiled it and gave it to Mr. Cerkez. I was present there. So he gave it to me. I knew most of the people who were mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So it was not you directly that -- rather, it was not Dr. Mujezinovic who gave this list directly to you but, rather, to Mario Cerkez; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, to the commander, Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were these persons released?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, the following morning, a number of them were released. For a number of them, the physician specialists were brought to see them from the health centre, and additional ones were also examined in the Vitez cinema hall, and I believe that three or four remained detained and were not released.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I see that your memory is different than that of Dr. Mujezinovic. I would like to then move on forward because, otherwise, we are on the periphery of the issue at trial. I would like for you to confirm for me, or for you to deny, what was stated in the statement of Dr. Mujezinovic in which he states -- first of all, his statement is located on page 1.713, the line from the bottom of the page, third-from-the-last line on the page, line 23. Here he states that the following day he was detained, on the night of the -- from the 19th to the 20th, that is to say, from Monday to Tuesday, and that the following day he was presented to Ivan Santic and Pero Skopljak. Ivan Santic and Pero Skopljak, both of these men, repeated the threat that was made by the HVO, that is, that all of the hostages would be killed if the Muslims were to advance. They also asked Dr. Mujezinovic to sign a joint document which Dr. Mujezinovic agreed to sign on the date which was -- that day, that is to say, the 20th of April, 1993. Does your information confirm the statement made by Dr. Mujezinovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At a meeting of the most prominent Muslims in Vitez which were detained in the cinema hall in Vitez, I remember several of those present: Fuad Kaknjo, president of the executive committee who was in the joint government; and then Muazem Gerim, who was a prominent citizen and business person; Nuraga Mulahalilovic, who was the director of the high school centre; Kadir Dzidic, who was also with the high school centre and he was the brother of Sefkija Dzidic who was the commander of the Territorial Defence; another prominent citizen, Batija Sivro, who is an engineer; and Dr. Mujezinovic was also present, and he had not been detained at that time anymore. They were all present, and they asked for a meeting with Pero Skopljak and Ivica Santic. I mediated in this. And in principle, I agreed with Ivica Santic and Pero Skopljak to hold this meeting. I'm not exactly sure of its time, but I believe it was around 2200 hours because then they thought that they would be able to make the meeting, which was to be held in an office in the Croatian centre. The Muslims whom I just mentioned I personally called, including Dr. Muhamed. We sat in this office, and I had no official business there, I was there just as a friend, and they were there waiting for Pero Skopljak and Ivan Santic. Since they were all my good acquaintances and fellow citizens and Dr. Muhamed was a friend among them and Muazem Gerim's daughter was a school friend with my daughter and they were best friends, I did not want to leave them alone, and I stayed there with them all night until 5.00 the next morning when Santic and Skopljak arrived, even though I could have gone home, but out of solidarity, I stayed with them. I brought them cigarettes, I brought them coffee, and I spent the whole night with them. In the morning -- apparently they were not able to make it sooner because they had meetings with international representatives and some military personnel -- eventually, Santic and Skopljak arrived, and I went home to sleep, and I was not present at this meeting between the two Croatian officials and the Muslim prominent citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cilic. I would now like to go on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 339.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Cilic, do you recall this joint statement signed here by Mr. Ivan Santic, a representative of the Croatian community, and Dr. Mujezinovic, a representative of the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I recall it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Dr. Mujezinovic indicated under what conditions he was led to sign this joint statement on the 20th of April, 1993, while he had been detained since the night before. I would like to call your attention, Mr. Cilic, to paragraph 4 of this joint statement. In paragraph 4, Mr. Cilic, it is stated that the Vance-Owen Plan should be implemented in Vitez and in Province 10 even before it is signed by the Serbian side. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no objection to the text of this statement, and I believe that it reflects the original form in which it was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I have perhaps one last question to ask you, Mr. Cilic. Do you not find that in the chaos of this day in April 1993 in Central Bosnia, that there is not a logical sense when we note that stated and constituted on the basis of an ideology of ethnic partitioning and that an opportunity presented itself during the negotiations in Geneva at the end of 1992 for this state to be able to claim guarantees for territory, and that the ultimatum I just talked about, that you yourself said you did not know the existence of, in which there were threats made to take by force this territory discussed in Geneva, if, by the 15th of April, they had not withdrawn their forces, and that in the month of April in 1993, and I am referring to a statement that was made here by Colonel Watters, who was the first, I believe, to testify for the Prosecution, he stated on this day in April there was a window of opportunity for the HVO, and he stated that the Muslim forces were occupied on the one front with the Serbs and also given the fact that the international media was occupied in Tuzla and therefore were not in the area and therefore knew nothing about what was happening in that area, both on television and on the ground. Do you not believe that given all these elements, that this chaos basically has a very clear sense, which is the action carried out by the HVO to guarantee itself an ethnically pure territory?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that this statement absolutely does not reflect those tenets. Knowing Ivica Santic as much as I do, he had problems with Croats because of his tolerance which he showed after tolerance became impossible, as well as Pero Skopljak, who always tended to -- always was leaning towards talks rather than a confrontation. I cannot believe that this statement reflects their views. Also, they were not of the level where they were able to implement these political goals. I think this reflects Ivo Santic's desire to keep peace in the area. He could be defined as a utopian type because he was trying to create an oasis of peace there, even though it was very clear to everyone that Bosnia could not be turned into an oasis of peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cilic. I request that the following documents be submitted, documents 332 to 339, be tendered as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I see no objection. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to the admission of Exhibit number 333, which is the Reuters report, which has not been authenticated at all, and we do not know whether it is admissible. Also, the witness did not recognise the contents of this exhibit. In addition, I believe it is the Exhibit 334, but let me tell you what it is, at 600 hours, so this is the report sent by the Jure Francetic Brigade. Perhaps the gentleman from the registry may assist me in confirming that I have written down the right exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, 334, yes. Why do you object to the admission of 334?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Again, the witness did not recognise the contents of this document. He said that he was not familiar with this document, he knew nothing of its contents, and the end of the document was not authenticated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The two documents will be admitted into evidence, but it will be, of course, for the Court to decide on the weight to be attached to them, and including, of the course, the Reuters report. It's just a press report, and we will duly take that into account. So, therefore, they are all admitted into evidence, but I would like also to ask the Prosecutor whether he has made up his mind about the exhibits tendered by Defence counsel, D35/2, D40/2, 41/2, 42/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, in regards to these documents, we have no explanation with regards to the actual sequencing of numbers, and we hope that the witness will be able to give us an explanation about the way in which these numbers were assigned. However, that was not the case. It seems that the content itself of these documents are absolutely in contradiction with what we have learned about that situation through testimony received by this Tribunal from British officers who were posted in Vitez. Consequently, it seems that given this failure to explain this inconsistency, and given the date on which this document was submitted, we request that this Tribunal allow me to reserve my answer until other witnesses can give us other information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We decided to admit into evidence these four documents, and again, it will be for the Court to decide on their probative value. So they are admitted into evidence. We may now move on to the re-examination of this witness. If you agree, I intend to make a break at 12.15. So you have half an hour. We have a 15-minute break and resume at half past twelve. Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a request. I request that you allow additional examination of the witness by the counsel which had not originally cross-examined him, because in the cross-examination certain issues were raised that they would like to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we can't admit that. The witness may be re-examined by those Defence counsel who proceeded to the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: These exhibits have been admitted. I'm referring to documents 41 -- they have been admitted into evidence. However, you raised the question during the examination-in-chief, and I would now like to ask the witness about it, because I subsequently noticed some differences in these documents. So could we show these two documents to the witness, D40/2 and D41/2. These documents, could they be shown to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you look how these documents were marked. On one hand, document 40/2 carries a number, strictly confidential number. So there is an indication. On the other side is number 02-125/9. You said that you can't explain how these numbers are formed. However, my question is: Is this strictly confidential number entered in one register and the regular number in another register?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly that must be the case. I know that for sure, but I don't know anything else about the methodology.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Is that perhaps the reason why there is a difference between the numbers that President Cassese noted in the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably that is the reason. That appears to be clear to me too now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: May I also ask you, I have examined these documents of the Vitez Brigade. Do you perhaps recall whether this first indication you have in both the numbers, does the first number refer to a certain person? For example, the commander would be 1 and then the lower ranks would have higher numbers? Do you know this or not?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I have been thinking about this. It could be the case but I cannot assert that. Perhaps if I had several reports and could compare a number of them I might be able to conclude something about the numbering, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Another question, that is the difference -- it was an objection on the part of the Prosecution. Could you explain, does the Vitez Brigade have a separate system of numbers and the Operative Zone command another set of numbers used by the commands of the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question? I didn't quite follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Are there two separate systems of numbering, one set being used by the Vitez Brigade and another set by the command of the Operation Zone and Colonel Blaskic, or do they use the same numbers?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Vitez Brigade had its own register.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So it is not possible to compare the sequence of dates, nor the sequence of numbers, because each used a separate system of numbering and entering documents into the logbook?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had a brigade secretary who had two books, or logbooks, or registers in which only the Vitez Brigade documents were registered. Then there was a book in which we registered incoming documents but not outgoing documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could the Prosecution Exhibit 335 be shown to the witness again, please? Paragraph 3 saying that in the period from the 16th of April until the 28th of April a total of 498 conscripts were mobilised, who were actively included in the HVO units. Most of the conscripts mobilised from the beginning of the outbreak of the conflict were directly sent to the front defence lines. The same being used as replacements after the response to the first blow, which means that they are gradually included as replacements for soldiers belonging to the mobile units. Can you please look at this list once again and tell us, in view of the fact that this mentioned from the 16th to the 28th of April, who among these people were mobilised on the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have any such information in my mind, and I cannot conclude from this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: As for the other dates, the 20th, 21st through until the 28th of April, was anyone mobilised on those dates according to this list? Can you see that from this list?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My answer is the same as to your previous question; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this mobilisation occurred in the period from the 16th until the 28th of April, is it visible from this list how this mobilisation actually took place? Are you thinking of who was mobilised on what date?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. That cannot be seen from this list. That is why in my response to the Prosecutor I said that they were mobilised until the 28th, but when exactly cannot be concluded from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell us, in view of the fact that you were in the command of the Vitez Brigade, do you know how the mobilisation was carried out? Would a person mobilise people carrying lists, were summonses handed in or was it simply done on the spot with people being called in as replacements?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In such a chaotic situation, there was no question of the formal type of mobilisation. What we did was to recruit as many people as possible as quickly as possible, even untrained people without uniforms, without asking whether anyone was sick or not, simply to ask them to come to the frontlines because the situation was critical for Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was any list at all of the reservists that would be updated on a daily basis so that people would know who was where, who was doing what and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. There were no such lists, nor did we have such an administration that could keep all these records and update them daily. All the necessary institutions had not been established, and when I say that, I mean the administration of the brigade too was lacking.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Does that mean that it was not possible to establish who was mobilised on which day as there were no lists, there were no official call-up papers, there were no public mobilisation proclamations as far as you know? Were there any?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think there was no public mobilisation announcement in those days still, but nor did we know exactly -- I assume -- of course I'm not quite sure, but I think it was -- these lists were compiled on the basis of reports of commanders from the front. People hid. Everybody tried to dodge recruitment. Most people didn't want the war. Most people were afraid. The vast majority had never experienced war, and the structure was not such that everything could be legally carried out and in a proper way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, when asked whether you knew whether Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic had been mobilised by the 16th, you said that they had not.

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know how and when they were mobilised later on?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the Prosecution Exhibit 337 once again? This document was compiled by Stipo Krizanac, head of the Defence Department. It doesn't carry a date, but clearly it was in 1994, because on page 1 he mentioned the date in 1994. What do you think?

utterances.speaker: ZVONIMIR CILIC (Resumed)
